transcript_body:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-07-21 | Start time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood CSM), Hannah Li (Redwood Legal); Marta Ruiz (Opaline Procurement), Devon Lee (Opaline Security), Sanjay Patel (Eng Lead), Renee O'Neill (Opaline Legal), Tom Burns (FinOps)

[00:00:00] Jared Kim: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have a pretty packed agenda, i can run a quick orientation then hand off to Priya for the technical bits and then we'll go through legal / procurement questions. Marta, thanks for coordinating on your side.

[00:00:24] Marta Ruiz: Thanks Jared. Quick note, we've got Renee from legal and Tom from finops on because procurement wants clarity on the MSA exceptions and the pricing approval path. We need to understand any non-standard clauses up front.

[00:00:45] Priya Malhotra: Hi all, Priya here. I'll cover deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), and specifically how KMS and SSO would work for your on-prem and VPC options.

[00:01:10] Renee O'Neill: Couple of immediate asks: Does Redwood accept our redlines to the indemnity and data residency sections? Also, we need SOC2 and encryption proof.

[00:01:27] Jared Kim: Got it. High level: Redwood supports three deployment options — Hosted API for fast onboarding, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For regulated PHI workflows we typically recommend Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS. But we can discuss exceptions.

[00:01:52] Tom Burns: From finance, pricing is the main gating item. We need a predictable unit economics model for the pilot and a clear path to scale with committed capacity or reserved capacity pricing. Also curious about any egress fees.

[00:02:15] Devon Lee: On security, we need to confirm encryption at rest, KMS integration options, and audit logs retention. We have a 7-year retention policy for some logs, and want to know how that maps to your observability retention tiers.

[00:02:37] Priya Malhotra: For KMS you can either bring your own KMS (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS and on-prem HSM via standard interfaces). In Private deployments the customer key never leaves their VPC. On audit logs: we offer configurable retention tiers — default 90 days, extended retention as an add-on. We'll put concrete numbers in the follow-up note.

[00:03:05] [timestamp gap — 20s small cross-talk] Hannah Li: We also have the standard SOC2 Type II and security package. I'll attach our security pack and a compliance matrix after.

[00:03:28] Sanjay Patel: Quick question on model fallbacks and data caching — for latency-sensitive workflows do we get guarantees that KV cache won't leak PII? Are there options to disable caching per-route?

[00:03:48] Priya Malhotra: Good call out. We support per-route cache controls; you can disable prefix/KV caching for routes handling PII. For Private deployments there's an option to encrypt KV cache with your keys. I'll include that in the tech note.

[00:04:10] Jared Kim: On the MSA/DPA front, historically we see three common exceptions: indemnity cap, data residency clauses, and audit/inspection scope. Renee, can you share the specific line items you're expecting to change?

[00:04:28] Renee O'Neill: We'll share an initial redline list. The big ones are: 1) broader indemnity carve-outs for subcontractors; 2) more prescriptive data residency guarantees — specifically EU and US segmented hosting; 3) clarity on breach notification timelines.

[00:04:46] Jared Kim: Understood. Our legal team tends to be amenable to narrowing indemnity language and clarifying breach timelines. Photo: we'll need to check DPA specifics around subprocessor lists. Hannah will cover that.

[00:05:04] Hannah Li: On subprocessors, we maintain a public list and provide 30 days notice for additions; for private deployments we can allow a confined list as part of the contract.

[00:05:25] Tom Burns: Pricing again — what's the pilot commitment vs reserved capacity delta? For pilot do we expect variable per-token billing, and then a transition to a commit with a monthly minimum?

[00:05:38] Jared Kim: Typically pilot uses metered billing with a soft cap to prevent surprises; if you choose Dedicated the model moves to committed monthly throughput at discounted unit costs. We'll supply a pricing ladder in the follow-up.

[00:05:55] Marta Ruiz: Procurement needs to see sample SOW and acceptance criteria for the pilot before we sign anything. Is that something you can share?

[00:06:06] Carlos Vega: Yes — Carlos here — i'll create a concise pilot SOW that includes acceptance tests (latency p95, throughput, and quality checks against an eval set). We'll tailor it to Opaline's clinical latency target.

[00:06:25] Sanjay Patel: Our target: 100ms p95 for short form responses in the EU region. What do we typically hit for Private deployments?

[00:06:36] Priya Malhotra: Private in-region can meet that with the right GPU-backed nodes and tuned batching. For hosted we have predictable benchmarks but they depend on model and prompt size. We'll propose two target SLAs: one for pilot (best-effort with monitoring), and production SLA with uptime credit and latency SLO.

[00:06:58] Devon Lee: About SLA credits — what's the formula? Also do you offer financial credits or service days?

[00:07:08] Jared Kim: SLA credits are typically service credits applied to monthly invoices. Formula is uptime shortfall percentage multiplied by a contractual cap. We can share our standard SLA language; non-standard caps may be negotiated in enterprise contracts.

[00:07:28] Renee O'Neill: We might need a lower cap on liability and stronger uptime credits given we are processing patient-facing triage flows. We'll flag that for the redline session.

[00:07:41] Tom Burns: Also egress and data transfer fees — redwood, do you bill for egress between regions or for logs export?

[00:07:51] Priya Malhotra: There may be network egress costs when moving data between regions; we try to absorb intra-region traffic in dedicated setups but will call out any cross-region transfers in the pricing attachment. Logs export for audit might be included up to a limit, after which extra archival fees apply.

[00:08:18] [00:08:18] Marta Ruiz: Procurement process question: We have a three-step internal approval: Procurement sign-off, Legal redline acceptance, and Finance commit. Each step takes 1-2 weeks. We need a clear escalation path if approvals slip.

[00:08:36] Jared Kim: Good to know. We can assign a Redwood internal champion and a legal POC. I, Jared, will be the external point, Priya will be the technical champion, and Hannah will be Redwood legal's point. For escalations we usually have a predefined SLAs playbook and executive sponsor loop.

[00:08:55] Renee O'Neill: Will you accept our standard vendor questionnaire and the SOC2 + penetration test artifacts?

[00:09:06] Hannah Li: Yes. We can accept vendor questionnaire, and will provide SOC2 attestation and pen test summary. Full pen test report can be shared under NDA if needed.

[00:09:20] Sanjay Patel: A little nuance on KMS — if we bring our keys, is there any performance hit? We need to know if crypto operations will add latency to token serving.

[00:09:31] Priya Malhotra: There is minimal overhead; we use envelope encryption patterns so the per-token critical path is not dominated by KMS calls — keys are cached securely in the HSM/KMS. We'll describe the flow and benchmarks in the tech note.

[00:09:53] Tom Burns: For the pricing approval path — who signs commercial exceptions on Redwood's side? Do we get an exec approval or is it the legal ops team?

[00:10:04] Jared Kim: Commercial exceptions are approved by sales leadership in conjunction with legal and finance. For enterprise deals we usually get a pricing binder and a commercial approver. If there are large deviations we'll need a sponsor on your side to keep timelines.

[00:10:20] Marta Ruiz: Our timeline: we'd like a pilot to start in August, procurement signed by mid-August, and production go-live in September. Is that realistic?

[00:10:30] Jared Kim: It's aggressive but feasible. Key dependencies: timely redline responses from Opaline legal, finance sign-off on pricing, and a short technical pilot prep. If procurement can turn the intake form in this week that helps.

[00:10:50] Devon Lee: About data residency: we need EU data to stay in EU for regulated workflows. Can you guarantee region pinning?

[00:11:00] Priya Malhotra: Yes. For Private you can pin to region and we can deploy nodes in EU only. For hosted we also allow region routing policies and pinned model instances for enterprise tiers. We'll document the routing policy and fallback behavior.

[00:11:20] Renee O'Neill: Also auditability: we need a record of data access and admin activity for 7 years. What's Redwood's longest retention offering for audit logs?

[00:11:33] Hannah Li: We currently offer extended audit log retention tiers up to 7 years as an enterprise add-on. We'll include cost estimates.

[00:11:50] Carlos Vega: On pilot acceptance — suggested tests: 1) latency p95 under 150ms for sample prompts; 2) throughput 50 qps sustained for 10 minutes; 3) QA pass rate on dev prompt set at threshold X. We'll align that to Opaline's acceptance criteria in the SOW.

[00:12:12] Sanjay Patel: For the QA pass rate, we need to ensure the evaluation harness is deterministic. Does Redwood provide evaluation tooling or do we run our own?

[00:12:22] Carlos Vega: We'll provide the eval harness and can run it jointly with your team. The results will be included in the pilot report.

[00:12:36] Tom Burns: Any reference customers with healthcare deployments we can speak to about contractual protections?

[00:12:44] Jared Kim: We can provide references; i'll flag a couple of redwood customers in the healthcare space, pending permission from them.

[00:12:55] Marta Ruiz: Ok let's recap action items. Jared, you'll share an annotated MSA and the pricing ladder by Friday. Priya will share KMS and region pinning technical notes and a deployment diagram. Carlos will send a pilot SOW. Hannah will attach the SOC2 and compliance pack. Tom will circulate internal procurement checklist. Renee will send initial MSA exception list.

[00:13:26] Renee O'Neill: For the legal workshop, we prefer a 60-minute redline session with track-changes in the doc. Renee will lead on Opaline's side and Hannah will lead for Redwood.

[00:13:40] Jared Kim: Great. We'll schedule a legal redline workshop for early next week. I'll send a calendar invite after the call.

[00:13:50] [closing chatter — confirmations and goodbyes]

[00:14:05] Jared Kim: Thanks everyone, we will follow up with the attachments and proposed times. Feel free to reach out if anything else comes up.

[00:14:15] Marta Ruiz: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes about transcription: occasional words mis-captured (e.g., Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as Redwood Dedicatede), brief crosstalk, and some acronyms slightly off in the auto transcript. Attachments mentioned: security pack, pilot SOW, pricing ladder, annotated MSA/DPA.

End of transcript.
